title: Runtime error taxonomy and retry-hint adapter for SDKs
creator: Aisha Park
description: Define and implement a cross-language error taxonomy and a small runtime adapter (Retry-Hint Adapter) that maps raw server/runtime failures to consistent, actionable SDK exceptions and machine-readable retry hints for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This ticket covers the taxonomy, adapter design, canonical error codes, streaming resumability hints, and examples for developers integrating retries and backoff strategies.
acceptance_criteria: A documented error taxonomy with at least three classification buckets (transient, permanent, unknown) and a short rationale for each classification.

A Retry-Hint Adapter library implemented idiomatically in Python/TS/Go that consumes server error payloads and emits: standardized SDK exception classes, a numeric error_code, and a retry_hint object (retryable: true|false, suggested_backoff_ms: integer, idempotency_required: boolean, resumable_stream_token: optional string).
Unit and integration tests covering 95% of adapter logic including streaming resume cases and malformed server payloads.
Examples added to SDK docs showing recommended retry loops for blocking calls and streaming reads across Python/TS/Go.
A migration note for existing users explaining behavioral changes and guidance for opt-out (if any).
design_notes: Goal: keep runtime adapter lightweight; canonical mapping must be deterministic and easy to reason about when debugging production incidents.
We will not rely on new server-side contracts; adapter must tolerate both older error payloads (message, code) and richer modern payloads (error_code, hints, request_id).

Classification bands: transient (retry w/ backoff), fatal (do not retry, surface actionable message), soft-fallback (retry to alternate model/region), unknown (treat as transient by default but include verbose telemetry).
Streaming: provide resumable_stream_token when KV cache or partial sequence can be resumed; SDKs must attach 'x-redwood-resume-token' header on re-open where provided.
User-facing message pattern: short actionable summary + suggested next step + link to docs (where appropriate).
implementation_plan: Draft canonical error_code list (numeric) and human-readable keys in documentation page.
Implement Retry-Hint Adapter core in the monorepo as a small language-agnostic spec file (YAML) + language bindings that load the spec at build-time.
Python: create exceptions.RedwoodRetryHint and extend existing SDK exceptions to include .retryable and .suggested_backoff_ms fields.
TypeScript: extend Error types with typed RetryHint interface, include helper isRetryable(err) and getBackoffMs(err).
Go: add a RetryHint struct returned by helper WrapError(err) and provide IsRetryable(err) and SuggestedBackoff(err) helpers.
Add streaming helpers: ResumeTokenStore interface + CLI flag to emit resume token in debug logs for troubleshooting.
Integrate telemetry: ensure adapter attaches stable telemetry keys: error_code, classification, server_request_id, adapter_version.
Create PRs and coordinate with runtime and server teams for any missing server hint fields (non-blocking if absent).
test_plan: Unit tests for mapping table entries and fallback behavior when unknown fields are present.
Simulation tests for transient spike: confirm SDK retry loop respects suggested_backoff_ms and stops after configurable attempts.
End-to-end integration test with hosted API to validate resumable streaming scenario (server issues disconnect at token boundary and provides resume token).
Cross-language smoke tests to ensure parity between Python/TS/Go adapters.
Load test to ensure adapter code path does not add measurable latency (<1ms median per error path).
rollout_plan: Merge feature flags into each SDK repo and gate behavioral change behind opt-in config 'enable_retry_hints'.
Release minor SDK versions with adapter behind flag; collect telemetry on adoption and misclassifications for two weeks.
Enable by default in sdks-2026.04 after initial telemetry review, publish migration notes and sample patterns.
Announce to customers via changelog with examples and troubleshooting guidance.
Follow-up: add console dashboards for misclassified errors and unusual retry storm patterns.
sample_mappings: 1002 -> rate_limit: transient, suggested_backoff_ms=500, idempotency_required=true, note='Consider exponential backoff and jitter'
2001 -> model_incompatible: fatal, suggested_backoff_ms=0, idempotency_required=false, action='Pin model or fall back to compatible variant'
3001 -> kv_cache_mismatch: soft-fallback, suggested_backoff_ms=100, resumable_stream_token provided when available
docs_examples: Python example: try/except pattern showing usage of e.retryable and e.suggested_backoff_ms, plus sample backoff helper.
TypeScript example: await call(); catch (err) { if (isRetryable(err)) await backoff(getBackoffMs(err)); }
Go example: if redwood.IsRetryable(err) { time.Sleep(redwood.SuggestedBackoff(err)) ; retry() }
Streaming example (all langs): on disconnect, if ResumeToken present -> reopen stream with header 'x-redwood-resume-token' and validate sequence continuity.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: misclassification causing unnecessary retries -> Mitigation: conservative default (unknown->treat as transient but with telemetry tag) and opt-out flag.
Risk: increased SDK surface leads to user confusion -> Mitigation: short, opinionated guidance + code samples and an 'escape hatch' config to return raw server payload.
Risk: telemetry leak of PII in verbose error messages -> Mitigation: scrub messages server-side and only include non-sensitive fields in adapter telemetry.
